witness.text:
Saving every remaining dollar at 7% she
gets there in 33 years

comparisons.rationale: $635 a month at 7% (monthly compounding) to $965,000 takes 32.8 years; $38,580 a year (3,215 x 12) matches "about 38,600", and 25 x $38,600 is $965,000. Compounding is nominal 7% against a 25x spending target in constant dollars, which the video itself flags ("that 5% real return is doing unpaid labor").
comparisons.uncertainty: Arithmetic recomputed; real versus nominal not reconciled in the script.

witness.text:
which pulls
33 years down to 22

comparisons.rationale: Raising savings to $1,100 a month at 7% reaches $965,000 in 25.9 years, not 22; lowering the target with the $350 rent cut (25 x $34,400 = $860,000) gives about 24.6 years; 22 years would need about $1,545 a month for $965,000 or $1,377 a month for $860,000. A reduced target that also treats the state-tax saving as spending is not supported (the budget lines contain no tax).
comparisons.uncertainty: Arithmetic recomputed; state tax saving not given.

financial_checks.claim: Delia: $635 a month at 7% to $965,000 takes 33 years
financial_checks.result: 32.8 years (monthly compounding); 33.8 with annual contributions. Budget lines sum to $3,215; leftover $635; 25 x $38,580 = $964,500.

financial_checks.claim: With rent cut $350 and no state income tax, $635 becomes $1,100 and 33 years becomes 22
financial_checks.result: $1,100 a month takes 25.9 years to $965,000 (24.6 if the target also falls to $860,000). 22 would need about $1,377-$1,545 a month.

financial_checks.claim: Mr. Money Mustache table at 5% real: 10% saved is 51 years, 50% is 17, 75% is 7
financial_checks.result: 51.4, 16.6, 7.1. Hold. The video says "drop it to two and 17 years quietly becomes a lot more": at 2% real, 50% saving takes 20.5 years.
$714,286 and $1,142,857; the gap is $428,571. Delia is described as "already there" at $38,600, but her 25x number used 4%; at 3.5% it is $1.10M.

financial_checks.claim: Roman: $12,900 monthly take-home, $100,000 spending, "4500 a month" saved, 35%; saves seven times Delia on four times the income
financial_checks.result: $54,800 saved (35.4%) = $4,567 a month; 7.2x Delia; income ratio 3.9. Hold.

financial_checks.claim: Median household income $83,700; average spending $78,500; implied savings rate about 6%
financial_checks.result: 6.2%, but median income against mean spending is not a like-for-like base.

financial_checks.claim: Premium cliff: 60-year-old couple over 400% of poverty "looking at roughly 22,600 a year in premiums"; about 4 million lose coverage
financial_checks.result: KFF (30 September 2025, via search summaries) projected a premium increase of more than $22,600 for a 60-year-old couple at $85,000 (402% of poverty); the video's wording drops "increase".

financial_checks.claim: Safe withdrawal: Bengen 4.15% (1994), Kitces 3.5% at 45 years, 21 countries 3-3.5%, Morningstar 3.9%, Bengen now 4.7%, 4% rule leaves more than double the start in two thirds of periods, 3.5% over 50 years ends at nine times half the time
financial_checks.result: Only Morningstar's 3.9% (2026, 90% over 30 years) was located in search-result summaries; Bengen 4.15%/4.7%, Kitces, 21-country and nine-times figures are analyst recall.

financial_checks.claim: Market did roughly 13% a year in 2010-2021
financial_checks.result: About 12.9% (price) or 15.2% (total return), computed from annual S&P 500 returns recalled by the analyst, not re-fetched.

financial_checks.claim: Vanguard 2026 median 401(k) $44,115, average $167,970; Federal Reserve 46% of households have no retirement account; AARP 28% retired too early; 7% returned to work
financial_checks.result: Not re-verified here; the same Vanguard pair recurs in `0J8MtFWsWY8` from the same channel (not independent evidence).

financial_checks.claim: "Roman hits his coast number in two years. Delia needs 11"; barista "a 40% cut in withdrawals"
financial_checks.result: No inputs are given for the 2 and 11 years (for Delia at 34 with $635 a month at 7%, a $197,000-style coast target takes about 10.6-13.3 years depending on the target age), so the figures cannot be audited; $15,000 of $40,000 is a 37.5% cut.

strengths: Unifying equation and a genuinely clarifying kitchen-table example whose arithmetic mostly reproduces.
Self-critical evidence section (survivorship, sequence risk, 6% savings rate, unspent wealth).
A closing action that is small and measurable (the coast number).
weaknesses: The "22 years" geoarbitrage payoff is not reproduced.
Garbled 72(t) line and an unattributed "$22,600" total.
Thumbnail types and title "every" outrun the script.
Two community pitches inside a retirement-math video.
contradictions: "The one thing I'd want you to take" (coast) versus "the most important sentence in this video" (nine times).
"The failure mode I promised you at the start" versus an opening that only loosely plants it ("almost nobody pulls it off") without naming unspent wealth.
25x spending at 4% versus lean FIRE costed at 3.5%.
"RETIRE NOW!?" versus the video's argument that this is mostly out of reach.
improvement_opportunities: Fix the geoarbitrage payoff: show Delia's years at $1,100 a month (25.9) and, separately, with a lower target (24), in one on-screen table.
Name Traditional and Expat FIRE in the script or replace those two icons with Lean and Flamingo so the thumbnail matches the content.
State the 22,600 as the premium INCREASE (KFF, 60-year-old couple at 402% of poverty) and put the source on screen.
Replace "the failure mode I promised you at the start" with a real early plant ("the way this fails is the opposite of what you expect") so the callback pays.
Drop one of the two community pitches or move it after the closing action.
